statement: AoE2DE AI is consumed through an .ai/.per script loading and rule execution substrate.
The native executable exposes scheduler vocabulary involving rule IDs, sorted rule indices, priorities, intervals, enable/disable state, and execution diagnostics.
Goals, strategic numbers, timers, and facts form persistent/observable components of the AI decision substrate.
Native/UP interfaces must be classified by evidence strength; embedded strings alone do not prove complete semantics.
XS capabilities are not ByzBot implementation dependencies and are not Layer 1 completion gates; XS evidence may remain machine archaeology only.
Execution failure and invalid scheduler operations are observable diagnostic conditions and must be represented in production architecture.
Validator corpus expectations and target-engine runtime semantics may differ and must be analyzed separately when an identifier is disputed.
A robust runtime architecture should conceptually separate observation, state/belief, intent, authorization, execution, verification, and recovery.
The native AI corpus contains an explicit 'Init AI Facts' diagnostic boundary followed by comparison and player-scope fact vocabulary.

The native AI semantic corpus includes game-mode, player, civilization, map-size, victory, age, difficulty, resource-setting, and processing-mode vocabulary around game-start and AI-fact initialization.
UP-PROCESS-60FPS is an explicit native AI-visible symbol; its relationship to rule-evaluation cadence is unresolved.
AI argument handling should be modeled as semantic resolution and validation before operation/result, rather than as unchecked integer passing.
Native feasibility answers machine executability, while strategic .per logic must determine desirability; these concerns should remain separate in ByzBot authority design.

Persistent-fact freshness should be tested with controlled direct-state and derived/feasibility observations to distinguish live evaluation, scheduler refresh, cached persistence, and fact-class-specific refresh models.

The controlled PE contains 166,741 physical .pdata runtime-function slots, of which 166,730 are non-zero records and 11 are trailing zero padding; valid starts are unique and monotonically ordered with no interval overlaps in the tested image.
The valid .pdata runtime-function intervals cover 45,879,189 bytes, approximately 88.88% of .text raw size; this is structural function geometry, not a semantic source-level function count.

The executable embeds CodeView RSDS data identifying PDB GUID b04f37aa-ccf9-48da-ad19-583ffb4bb36d with age 1; no matching local PDB was established, so the PDB remains an unauthenticated future lead until GUID/age verification.

Full .text Capstone scanning found zero RIP-relative references to seven selected AI diagnostic/source anchor addresses, and executable-wide exact 64-bit pointer scanning found zero occurrences of those addresses.

A correctly mapped metadata-area pointer to .pdata-recognized function 0x1417FF3E0 was rejected as an XS API implementation association after direct disassembly showed cleanup/destructor-like behavior.
Metadata proximity, a valid pointer, and valid .pdata function membership are insufficient to establish semantic API ownership; caller/callee, data ownership, and state-effect evidence are required.

The preferred native archaeology sequence is verified function geometry -> validated instruction body -> state/data read-write analysis -> branches/calls -> downstream consequence, with strings serving as subsystem anchors rather than primary proof.
Rule/fact/goal state, UnitAI order/action state, and simulation state may operate on distinct temporal cadences; this predicts possible observation staleness and command latency but remains unproven.
